2608.24848.title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
2608.24848.paper_summary: Web agents that act from rendered pixels avoid the fragility and heavy token cost of reading a page's HTML or accessibility tree, but training them depends on large amounts of high-quality interaction trajectories, and how to produce such data at scale remains an open problem. Public datasets typically contain only a few thousand trajectories drawn from a fixed and narrow set of websites, and even recent automated synthesis pipelines stay bound to predefined site lists or tutorial sources, so the number of distinct websites the agent ever sees barely grows. We present BrowserForge, a framework that generates web interaction data at scale by driving many browser sandboxes in parallel over the open web. BrowserForge couples three components: an open-web sourcing stage that exposes the agent to hundreds of thousands of real, openly reachable websites; a sandbox cluster manager that schedules hundreds of concurrent browsers with high utilization; and a Proposer-Solver dual-agent loop that turns a raw page into an executable task and then collects a verified trajectory for it. A rule-plus-model cleaning pipeline removes failed runs and rewrites the surviving reasoning into a single unified chain-of-thought style. Page structure such as the accessibility tree is used only as a synthesis-time signal; the agent we train and release acts purely from the screenshot. The resulting corpus contains 203,238 trajectories, each collected from a distinct website, larger and more diverse than prior trajectory datasets. Fine-tuning a compact multimodal model on this corpus raises its success rate on the live Online-Mind2Web from 25.66% to 33.33% and consistently improves step accuracy on the static Multimodal-Mind2Web, with the gain growing as the corpus scales. Controlled analyses further confirm that open-web sourcing and broad website coverage are key contributors to the observed improvement.
2608.24848.paper_summary_zh: 網路代理從渲染的像素中行動，避免了讀取頁面 HTML 或可及性樹的脆弱性和高昂的令牌成本，但訓練它們依賴於大量高質量的互動軌跡，而如何大規模產生這些數據仍然是一個未解決的問題。公共數據集通常僅包含從固定且狹窄的網站集提取的幾千條軌跡，即使是最近的自動合成管道也仍然受限於預定義的網站列表或教程來源，因此代理所見的不同網站數量幾乎沒有增長。我們提出了 BrowserForge，一個通過在開放網絡上並行驅動多個瀏覽器沙盒來大規模生成網絡互動數據的框架。BrowserForge 結合了三個組件：一個開放網絡來源階段，將代理暴露於數十萬個真實的、可公開訪問的網站；一個沙盒集群管理器，調度數百個高利用率的並發瀏覽器；以及一個提議者-解決者雙代理循環，將原始頁面轉換為可執行任務，然後收集經過驗證的軌跡。一個規則加模型的清理管道去除失敗的運行，並將存活下來的推理重寫為單一的統一思考鏈。頁面結構，如可及性樹僅用作合成時的信號；我們訓練並釋放的代理純粹依賴於截圖。最終的語料庫包含 203,238 條軌跡，每條都來自不同的網站，比之前的軌跡數據集更大且更具多樣性。在這個語料庫上對一個緊湊的多模態模型進行微調，將其在實時 Online-Mind2Web 上的成功率從 25.66% 提升至 33.33%，並穩定地提高靜態 Multimodal-Mind2Web 的步驟準確性，隨著語料庫的擴大，增益不斷增加。受控分析進一步確認，開放網絡來源和廣泛的網站覆蓋是觀察到的改進的關鍵因素。
